XInput vs DirectInput: Controller Mapping Explained

By PadLab · Updated October 5, 2026 · 4 minute read

XInput and DirectInput describe different input paths used by Windows games and controller software. The distinction explains why one gamepad can show familiar labels in one application and numbered inputs in another.

XInput in plain language

XInput is commonly associated with Xbox-style buttons, standardized axes and trigger behavior. Games targeting XInput expect a familiar A/B/X/Y layout.

DirectInput in plain language

DirectInput is a broader interface that can expose many controllers and controls. A DirectInput device may report numbers without the standard layout used by PadLab’s diagram.

How PadLab handles mapping

When the browser reports mapping: standard, PadLab labels common buttons and uses axes 0/1 and 2/3 for stick plots. Without standard mapping, it retains raw data but disables invented stick assignments.

Troubleshoot an unexpected layout

  1. Check the controller mode and manufacturer instructions.
  2. Compare direct USB with Bluetooth.
  3. Check Steam Input or another virtual-controller remapper.
  4. Select the intended device in PadLab.
  5. Use raw axis details when standard mapping is unavailable.

See detection troubleshooting and the button test.

What mapping does not tell you

Mapping does not prove that a button, sensor, cable or motor is healthy. It describes how the browser presents controls; it cannot measure true latency or USB polling frequency.
